current_evidence: The council's short link watford.gov.uk/validationchecklist serves the same 'Development Management Validation Checklist for Planning Applications', and the government planning data register lists file/1395 as Watford's validation checklist (start date 2024-01-01). The document text itself carries no adoption or version date.

issues.detail: The List date 2026-05-01 comes from PDF CreationDate metadata, not from the document. The checklist text has no adoption, version or publication date. Internal references (Watford Local Plan 2021-2038, Biodiversity Gain Regulations 2024, 'further national requirements are also expected in late 2023') suggest it was written in 2023-24. The government planning data register gives a start date of 2024-01-01. The workbook should show the date as undated or about 2024, not May 2026.
issues.evidence: No header, footer or version date in the document; 'Further national requirements are also expected in late 2023 and all development must adhere to this.'; planning.data.gov.uk entity 20247 start-date 2024-01-01

issues.detail: Part B lists 21 local requirements, but the workbook captured only about 13 of them. Missing items and their triggers: (2) Planning Statement - all applications, proportionate to the proposal; (3) Housing Schedule - proposals with a residential element, including a housing trajectory; (4) Affordable Housing Statement - proposals providing affordable housing (at least 60% social rent); (6) Energy and Sustainability Statements - proposals subject to climate and sustainability policy, plus a BREEAM pre-assessment for major non-residential schemes; (8) Landscaping Plan - hard and soft landscaping; (9) Transport Statement/Assessment - developments generating significant movement (only the Travel Plan half was captured); (11) Land Contamination Assessment; (12) Wind Assessment - tall buildings, with wind tunnel or CFD testing likely for buildings of 30m or more; (13) Daylight, Sunlight and Overshadowing Assessment - applications including or near residential development; (21) Training, Skills and Employment Strategy - major development proposals.
issues.evidence: Part B: Local Requirements, items 1-21 (e.g. '12. Wind Assessment', '13. Daylight, Sunlight and Overshadowing', '21. Training, Skills and Employment Strategy')

issues.detail: Every captured requirement sits under Full planning with an 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning' note (e.g. Arboricultural, Drainage, Fire Statement, Heritage Statement, Noise, Viability). Householder, Listed building consent, Advertisement consent, Lawful development certificate, Outline, S73 and Non-material amendment are all marked '(none) - national requirements only'. That is wrong. The checklist's Part C matrix has rows that mark local items as required for Householder Applications (about 9 items), Listed Building Consent (about 10), Advertising Consent (about 5), Certificate of Lawful Development (about 6), Section 73 (about 9), Outline Applications and buildings in Conservation Areas. Part B item 1 (Streetscene Elevation) also names householder extensions that raise the ridge height.
issues.evidence: Part C matrix rows: 'Householder Applications', 'Listed Building Consent', 'Advertising Consent', 'Certificate of Lawful Development', 'Section 73 Minor Material Amendment Application', 'Outline Application'; item 1: 'all extensions to dwellings involving a raise in ridge height'

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are fragments that do not say when the item applies. Health Impact Assessment: 'types of Health Impact Assessments which may be appropriate: 1.' (the source trigger is major residential schemes of 100+ units, major transport infrastructure and other significant infrastructure). Heritage Statement: 'As a guide a Heritage Statement must: 7|Page' (the source trigger is applications affecting a heritage asset or its setting). Travel Plan: 'should provide a Travel Plan.' (the trigger is developments generating significant movement). Ventilation/Extraction: '...odours will not be discernible at the nearest residential property. 17.' (the trigger is restaurant/takeaway extraction and B2 uses raising odour issues). Fire Statement starts mid-sentence with 'more storeys'. Ecological survey is cut off mid-word. Noise gives only 'prepared by a suitably qualified acoustician' and no trigger.
issues.evidence: Part B items 10, 15, 16, 20 and the transport item; e.g. HIA 'major residential proposals of 100 or more units'

issues.detail: Two triggers misstate the threshold. Drainage Strategy/SuDS is given as 'requirement for SuDS in new developments', but the source requires a Surface Water Drainage Scheme only for developments of 10 or more dwellings and all major commercial developments. The Arboricultural Impact Assessment trigger leaves out the actual trigger, which is sites with a TPO, trees in a Conservation Area, or trees on or next to the site over 75mm diameter (AIA/AMS/TPP where significant trees are affected).
issues.evidence: Item 18 Surface Water Drainage Scheme: 'developments of 10 or more dwellings and all major commercial developments'; Item 7 Tree Survey: trees 'over 75mm in diameter'

issues.detail: The 'Schedule of works (listed building)' row has the trigger '(AIA), Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) and Tree Protection Plan (TPP).' That is the tree survey text, misclassified as a listed building schedule of works. It duplicates the Arboricultural row, and Part B has no schedule-of-works local requirement.
issues.evidence: Workbook trigger_excerpt '(AIA), Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) and Tree Protection Plan (TPP).' matches Part B item 7 Tree Survey and Report

issues.detail: The 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' row's excerpt is an exemption note, not a requirement trigger: it says the test was done through the Level 2 SFRA (2020) and 'may not be required again'. It belongs under the Flood Risk Assessment item.
issues.evidence: 'sequential and exception test through the Level 2 Strategic Flood Risk Assessment (2020) and this may not be required again.'

summary: The workbook link is Watford's current, working validation checklist, but the May 2026 date comes from PDF metadata and the document itself is undated (about 2024). The workbook misses about 10 of the 21 Part B local requirements and puts everything under Full planning, although the Part C matrix assigns items to householder, LBC, adverts, LDC and S73. Several triggers are garbled or misstate thresholds.
